name: Idiopathic Aplastic Anemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Aplastic Anemia Study Group Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of pancytopenia with at least two of the following: neutrophils <500/μL, platelets <20,000/μL, reticulocytes <60,000/μL
Bone marrow biopsy showing hypocellularity (<25% cellularity) without abnormal infiltration or fibrosis
Exclusion of other causes of bone marrow failure such as inherited marrow failure syndromes, myelodysplastic syndromes, and secondary aplastic anemia
Negative flow cytometry for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria clones
Normal cytogenetic analysis to exclude clonal hematologic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pancytopenia with at least two cytopenias plus bone marrow hypocellularity and exclusion of other causes of marrow failure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires comprehensive clinical, laboratory, and bone marrow evaluation to exclude secondary causes.

laboratory: Severe pancytopenia on complete blood count
Bone marrow biopsy showing hypocellularity without fibrosis or infiltration
Negative tests for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
imaging: Chest X-ray may show signs of infection
Abdominal ultrasound usually normal; used to exclude hepatosplenomegaly
other: Flow cytometry to exclude paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
Viral serologies to exclude secondary causes

distinguishingFeatures: Dysplastic changes in bone marrow cells
Flow cytometry positive for CD55/CD59 deficiency

redFlags: Severe neutropenia with recurrent or severe infections
Presence of constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or night sweats
references: Young NS. Aplastic anemia. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(17):1643-1656.
Tichelli A, et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of aplastic anemia. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2017;12(1):43.
